violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: RAW CHICKEN STORED ABOVE FISH AND LAMB IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED FOODS DURING INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: BUTTER SAUCE AT 43-47 IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC TRANSFERRED FOODS TO FREEZER FOR RAPID COOLING TO 41F OR BELOW.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restricted Use Pesticide, Conditions of use
violations.observation: Restricted, commercial use pesticides present in the facility are applied by the operator who is not a certified pesticide applicator: RAID INSECT SPRAY IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Because of their toxicity, restricted use pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD INSECTICIDE DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE ONLY CERTIFIED PEST CONTROL SERVICES AT ESTABLISHMENT.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.corrective_action: Relocate the insect control device so that it is not located over a food preparation area and dead insects are prevented from being falling on exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC RELOCATED DEVICE AWAY FROM FOODS PREPARATION AREAS, FOODS, CLEAN EQUIPMENT OR UTENSILS DURING INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW FISH, RAW BEEF, RAW SHELL EGGS STORED ABOVE COOKED CHICKEN AND PREPARED SAUCES IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REORGANIZE FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: BUTTER CHICKEN SAUCE AT 84F ON COUNTER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REHEAT FOODS TO 165F OR ABOVE BEFORE PLACING IN STEAM TABLE FOR HOT HOLDING AT 135F OR ABOVE.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: SPINACH, LENTILS, CHICKPEAS, CHAPALI KABOB, TANDOORI CHICKEN ALL PREPARED FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.,
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO APPLY APPROPRIATE DATE MARKING DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE. Rawal Kabob (Inspection Date: 04/15/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: WORKING CONTAINERS OF SALTS, SPICES AND SAUCES ON KITCHEN COUNTER.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE ALL WORKING CONTAINERS AND FOODS REMOVED FROM ORIGINAL PACKAGING ARE LABELED WITH AT LEAST THE. COMMON NAME.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers were observed reused for the storage of SPICES, BEANS, ETC..
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE TRANSFER FOODS TO FOOD SAFE CONTAINERS DESIGNED FOR CONTINUOUS CLEANING AND SANITIZING. COMPLIANCE WILL BE CONFIRMED BY NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE ENTER KITCHEN FROM OUTSIDE AND DONNED GLOVES WITHOUT WASHING HANDS TO START FOOD PREPARATION.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO REMOVE GLOVES AND WASH HANDS BEFORE DONNING CLEAN GLOVES. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in THE FOOD PREPARATION SINK.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO WASH HANDS AT HANDWASHING SINK ONLY. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning

violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO SET UP SANITIZING BASIN WITH SANITIZER SOLUTION OF APPROPRIATE CONCENTRATION IN 3 COMPARTMENT SINK FOR SANITIZING ALL DISHES. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: RAW LAMB IN CONTAINER OF WATER AT 55F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC RETURNED LAMB TO WALK IN REFRIGERATOR DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. CHICK PEAS AT 45F, KARACHAIE CHICKEN AT 43F, BUTTER SAUCE AT 44F IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR COOKED THE DAY BEFORE.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING. INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS MEET COOLING PARAMETERS OF 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: CHICK PEAS AT 45F, KARACHAIE CHICKEN AT 43F, BUTTER SAUCE AT 44F ALL IN COVERD CONTAINERS IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR COOKED THE DAY BEFORE.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE USE APPROPRIATE METHODS TO COOL FOODS TO MEET THE COOLING PARAMETERS.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: SERVING UTENSILS IN CONTAINER OF WATER AT 82F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC PLACED CONTAINER WITH UTENSILS ON STOVE TOP FOR HEATING.
